editorial_thesis: Today’s strongest fresh signal is that practical leverage is moving from novelty to operating substrate: agent trust, maintainable open-model deployment, executable engineering harnesses, and source-bounded knowledge work.

topic_groups.title: AI Agent Standards + Identity
topic_groups.selection_rationale: NIST refreshed its agent standards initiative on August 14, making identity, authorization, interoperability, and measurable security the clearest under-covered lane after several days of product-heavy agent coverage.

sources.title: NIST AI Agent Standards Initiative
sources.why_selected: Identity, authentication, interoperability, and security evaluation are explicit priorities.
sources.usefulness: Turn its pillars into a Buildn agent-readiness checklist.

sources.title: NCCoE Software and AI Agent Identity and Authorization
sources.why_selected: A primary project surface for applying identity standards to enterprise agent use cases.
sources.usefulness: Prototype ownership, grant, expiry, and revocation records.

sources.title: OWASP GenAI Security Project
sources.why_selected: Maintains practical threat and control guidance for generative and agentic systems.
sources.usefulness: Map tool permissions and prompt-injection controls to client reviews.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol specification
sources.why_selected: The protocol surface gives portability a concrete contract instead of a vendor promise.
sources.usefulness: Keep Buildn connectors spec-first and capability-scoped.

sources.title: CSA AI Safety Initiative
sources.why_selected: Security research frames governance gaps around visibility, ownership, and access.
sources.usefulness: Use as a second opinion when scoping enterprise pilots.

topic_groups.title: Open Models + Deployment Reality
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Open-model coverage has been absent from the recent archive, while Hugging Face published a fresh summer analysis that separates frontier excitement from the small-model deployment layer.

sources.title: State of Open Models: Summer 2026
sources.why_selected: The analysis shows downloads concentrated in small practical models while frontier releases attract attention.
sources.usefulness: Use deployment fit, derivatives, and ecosystem health as selection signals.

sources.title: Kimi K3 technical blog
sources.why_selected: A frontier open-weight release illustrates the gap between headline scale and realistic serving requirements.
sources.usefulness: Treat it as a research benchmark, not an automatic production candidate.

sources.title: vLLM documentation
sources.why_selected: The serving layer exposes the operational reality of batching, caching, quantization, and hardware fit.
sources.usefulness: Run a pinned local inference benchmark before vendor selection.

sources.title: llama.cpp repository
sources.why_selected: Small and quantized deployment remains the practical edge of the open ecosystem.
sources.usefulness: Test offline fallback and private document workflows.

sources.title: MLCommons MLPerf Inference
sources.why_selected: A standardized benchmark gives hardware and latency context beyond model marketing.
sources.usefulness: Record throughput, tail latency, and cost for comparable tasks.

topic_groups.title: Agent-First Engineering Environments
topic_groups.selection_rationale: OpenAI’s February engineering report is a durable but not previously covered primary source; it provides a concrete operating model for shifting human effort from code typing to legibility, feedback, and recovery.

sources.title: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
sources.why_selected: OpenAI reports a large internal build where agents generated code, tests, tooling, and documentation while humans shaped the harness.
sources.usefulness: Translate the pattern into a small Buildn pilot with measurable loops.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot agent mode documentation
sources.why_selected: Documents an agent surface built around repository tasks, pull requests, and review.
sources.usefulness: Compare the workflow to existing issue-to-PR delivery.

sources.title: OpenAI Codex CLI repository
sources.why_selected: The open client makes tools, approvals, and local execution inspectable.
sources.usefulness: Study permission boundaries and reusable repo instructions.

sources.title: Mabl: agents shipping across 75+ repos
sources.why_selected: Cross-repo dependency context is presented as a prerequisite for safe scale.
sources.usefulness: Use dependency maps as an explicit context artifact.

sources.title: SWE-bench
sources.why_selected: A task benchmark anchors coding-agent claims in reproducible repository work.
sources.usefulness: Build a tiny private eval set instead of relying on generic scores.

topic_groups.title: Knowledge Work + Personal Leverage
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Learning and memory have not appeared in the last several days; this lane returns to practical knowledge operations, but with source-bounded retrieval and freshness rather than another generic note-taking roundup.

sources.title: APQC Knowledge Management
sources.why_selected: APQC provides current KM practices, metrics, and maturity framing for knowledge reuse.
sources.usefulness: Borrow freshness, ownership, and reuse metrics for personal and client knowledge.

sources.title: Zettelkasten method overview
sources.why_selected: A durable method for atomic notes and linked retrieval remains useful when paired with source provenance.
sources.usefulness: Use atomic evidence notes for recurring client decisions.

sources.title: Obsidian Help: Properties
sources.why_selected: Structured properties make local-first notes queryable without forcing a hosted system.
sources.usefulness: Define source, confidence, status, and review dates.

sources.title: Zotero documentation
sources.why_selected: Reference management keeps citations and source files attached to claims.
sources.usefulness: Use it as the evidence boundary for research-heavy work.

sources.title: Readwise Reader
sources.why_selected: A capture-and-review surface shows the value of keeping highlights connected to a review loop.
sources.usefulness: Test only if review friction is lower than the current workflow.
